name: Farro

pros.title: chewy texture holds up in full meals
pros.explanation: It works in soups, salads, and grain bowls without turning to mush.

pros.title: batch-cooks into a practical meal base
pros.explanation: One pot can cover several meals and takes stronger toppings well.

pros.title: pearled farro is easier to cook
pros.explanation: Removing some outer bran shortens the cooking time and makes it more approachable.

cons.title: pearling strips away part of the bran
cons.explanation: That convenience costs some fibre and micronutrient potential.

cons.title: contains gluten
cons.explanation: It is not suitable for coeliac disease or a gluten-free diet.

cons.title: still needs cooking and planning
cons.explanation: It is less instant than rice or couscous and definitely is not grab-and-go.

sourceNotes: Production entry for plain pearled farro on a dry raw per-100g basis.
USDA FoodData Central supplies the canonical macros, starch, fibre, and minerals.
Required gaps were filled with exact-identity Google-discovered values and exact pearled-emmer composition data; no other-food nutrient profile is used.
Narration uses the selected production values directly while provenance preserves exact, derived, and estimated status.
